t: Plunder: The Last of the War in Europe, 1945
en: Veteran military historian Max Hastings returns to the final weeks of the Second World War in western Europe, taking his title from Montgomery's Rhine crossing of March 1945, Operation Plunder. He moves between generals and ordinary people: the seizure of the Remagen bridge, Nazi 'Werewolf' killers in Aachen, the Dutch famine, the liberation of Belsen, Patton's doomed raid to free his son-in-law and the last SAS mission, ending with the German surrenders. A running thread is why German soldiers kept fighting so fiercely when all was lost. For anyone who likes big history told through vivid human stories.
zh: 資深戰史作家 Max Hastings 帶你重返二戰喺西歐嘅最後幾個星期。書名取自 1945 年 3 月蒙哥馬利橫渡萊茵河嘅「掠奪行動」。佢喺將軍同普通人之間穿插：盟軍搶佔雷馬根大橋、納粹「狼人」喺亞琛暗殺市長、荷蘭大饑荒、解放貝爾森集中營、巴頓為救女婿而發動嘅失敗突襲，同 SAS 最後一次任務，一直講到德國投降。書中不斷追問：明知必敗，點解德軍仲咁死命頑抗？適合鍾意由真實人物故事睇大歷史嘅讀者。

reviews.d: Michela Wrong calls Hastings 'a natural storyteller' with strong material; some passages feel like a class teacher and linger on archives.
reviews.dz: 讚佢係天生說故事高手，材料扎實；但有時似老師說教，部分檔案太長。

reviews.d: Tyler Cowen says he benefited from every page, struck by how hard the Germans fought on the way down.
reviews.dz: Tyler Cowen 話每頁都有得着，驚訝德軍敗局已定仍死戰。

ken: Wars rarely end cleanly: some of the cruellest fighting and suffering of 1945 came after the outcome was already certain.
kzh: 戰爭好少乾淨利落咁完結：1945 年最慘烈嘅戰鬥同苦難，好多都發生喺勝負早已分明之後。

sources.title: The Spectator: The dark finale of the Second World War (Michela Wrong)
